advances: Proves the concurrent-fan inequality for every nondegenerate triangle.  The proof gives an exhaustive finite classification of the vertex sectors, does not assume that the fan point lies in the triangle, and treats vertices or edges on fan rays, empty caps, and half-full caps by an explicit constraint-preserving limit.  It makes no localization claim for arbitrary convex bodies.
author: mp_r75_cf_all_triangle_types
proof:
Normalize \(|T|=1\), and write \(p_i=c_i\).  The invertible linear map
\[
z\longmapsto (x,y)=(\ell _1(z),\ell _2(z))
\]
does not change area fractions.  Thus \(\ell _3=-x-y\).  Label the six open sectors in cyclic order by
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
A:\ x<0,\ y<0, &
B:\ x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y<0, &
C:\ x>0,\ y<0,\ x+y>0,\\
D:\ x>0,\ y>0, &
E:\ x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y>0, &
F:\ x<0,\ y>0,\ x+y<0.
\end{array}
\tag{1}
\]
Their cap-incidence columns, in the row order \(H_i=\{\ell_i\leq0\}\), are
\[
A=(1,1,0),\quad B=(0,1,0),\quad C=(0,1,1),\quad
D=(0,0,1),\quad E=(1,0,1),\quad F=(1,0,0).
\tag{2}
\]

We first prove the result when no vertex is on a fan line and
\[
p_1<\frac12,\qquad p_2<\frac12.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(p_1=0\), then \(\ell _1>0\) almost everywhere on \(T\).  On
\(\{\ell _3>0\}=\{x+y<0\}\) this forces \(y<0\), so
\[
1-p_3\leq p_2
\]
and the result follows.  The case \(p_2=0\) is symmetric.  We may therefore assume \(p_1,p_2>0\).

Let \(M\) be the \(3\times3\) zero-one matrix whose \(ij\)-entry records whether the \(j\)-th vertex is in \(H_i\).  The first two row sums are \(1\) or \(2\): sum \(0\) was just handled, while sum \(3\) would give \(p_i=1\).  If the third row sum is \(3\), then \(p_3=1\) and there is nothing to prove.  If it is \(0\), then \(\ell _3>0\) throughout \(T\), hence \(T\subset H_1\cup H_2\) and
\[
1\leq p_1+p_2<1,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus every row sum is \(1\) or \(2\).  Every column sum is also \(1\) or \(2\), because three nonzero real numbers with sum zero have one or two negative entries.

This gives a finite exhaustive classification.  Permuting the three vertices is harmless.  The only nontrivial dihedral symmetry preserving the distinguished role of \(p_3\) and the unordered pair \(\{p_1,p_2\}\) is \(x\leftrightarrow y\); it swaps rows \(1,2\), swaps \(B,F\), swaps \(C,E\), and fixes \(A,D\).  Modulo precisely these operations, the possible multisets of vertex sectors are
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\text{number of ones in }M&\text{representatives}\\ \hline
3&BDF\\
4&ADD,\ BDE,\ ABD,\ BBE,\ BCF\\
5&ACD,\ BCE,\ CCF,\ AAD,\ ABE\\
6&ACE.
\end{array}
\tag{4}
\]
For completeness, there are \(6,45,45,6\) matrices before quotienting in the four rows of (4).  When the total is \(3\) or \(6\), all row and column degrees are respectively \(1\) or \(2\), giving the permutation matrix and its complement.  When the total is \(4\), there is one double row and one double column.  If the double row is row \(3\), incidence or nonincidence with the double column gives \(ADD,BDE\).  If the double row is row \(1\) or \(2\), the double column is nonincident, incident also with the other constrained row, or incident also with row \(3\), giving \(BBE,ABD,BCF\).  Complementing these five matrices gives the five total-\(5\) representatives in (4).  This proves exhaustiveness without assuming that the common fan point belongs to \(T\).  In particular, every triangle with the fan point outside \(T\) is already included in (4).

We next give exact algebraic certificates for the twelve types.  For positive \(u,v\), parameterize the value triple \((\ell _1,\ell _2,\ell _3)\) in each sector by
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
A&(-u,-v,u+v)\\
B&(u,-u-v,v)\\
C&(u+v,-u,-v)\\
D&(u,v,-u-v)\\
E&(-u,u+v,-v)\\
F&(-u-v,u,v).
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
For a word \(XYZ\) in (4), assign \((a,b)\) to its \(X\)-vertex, \((c,d)\) to its \(Y\)-vertex, and \((e,f)\) to its \(Z\)-vertex in (5).

We use the following elementary cap formula.  If the three values of an affine function at the vertices are \(-r,s,t\), with \(r,s,t>0\), then its nonpositive cap is the corner triangle of area fraction
\[
\frac{r^2}{(r+s)(r+t)}.
\tag{6}
\]
If the values are \(-r,-s,t\), its nonpositive cap is the complement of the positive corner triangle and has area fraction
\[
1-\frac{t^2}{(t+r)(t+s)}.
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, on each of the two edges from the isolated vertex, the zero occurs at the corresponding ratio \(r/(r+s)\) or \(r/(r+t)\), and triangle area is the product of the two edge ratios.

For type \(XYZ\), apply (6) or (7) to the \(i\)-th coordinates in (5), and write
\[
p_i=\frac{N_i}{D_i}
\]
with the positive denominator \(D_i\).  Thus, in the one-negative case,
\[
N_i=r^2,\qquad D_i=(r+s)(r+t),
\]
and in the two-negative case,
\[
N_i=(t+r)(t+s)-t^2,\qquad D_i=(t+r)(t+s).
\]
Put
\[
Q_i=D_i-2N_i\qquad(i=1,2)
\tag{8}
\]
and
\[
\Gamma=N_3D_1D_2-D_3(D_1-N_1)(D_2-N_2).
\tag{9}
\]
The assumptions say \(Q_1,Q_2\geq0\), and the desired inequality is exactly \(\Gamma\geq0\), because its denominator is \(D_1D_2D_3>0\).

For nine of the types, the following table gives manifestly nonnegative polynomials \(P_1,P_2\) such that
\[
\Gamma=Q_1P_1+Q_2P_2+R.
\tag{10}
\]
After collecting like terms in \(\mathbb Z[a,b,c,d,e,f]\), the last column is the exact number of monomials of \(R\); every coefficient of \(R\) is a positive integer, and its smallest coefficient is \(1\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|l|c}
\text{type}&P_1&P_2&\#\operatorname{supp}R\\ \hline
BDE&abe(a+b)&abe^2&67\\
ABD&0&a^2df&50\\
ACD&0&0&92\\
BBE&e(2acf+ade+2adf+aef+bce+2bcf+cef)
&e(2acf+ade+aef+bce+cef+ef^2)&36\\
BCE&be^2(e+f)&be^2(b+e)&95\\
CCF&e^3f&ef(e+f)^2&91\\
AAD&0&0&39\\
ABE&c(e+f)(de+2ef+f^2)&c^2(af+de+2ef)&42\\
ACE&ce(ad+ae+af+be+bf)&ce(ac+bc+bd)&155.
\end{array}
\tag{11}
\]
This is an exact coefficient certificate, not a numerical sign check: the sector-value dictionary (5), the two cap rules (6)-(7), and the definitions (8)-(10) determine every coefficient by multiplication in \(\mathbb Z[a,b,c,d,e,f]\).  Thus (11) proves \(\Gamma\geq0\) for all nine listed types.

For type \(ADD\), formulas (5)-(7) give
\[
p_1=\frac{a^2}{(a+c)(a+e)},\qquad
p_2=\frac{b^2}{(b+d)(b+f)},
\]
\[
p_3=1-\frac{(a+b)^2}
{(a+b+c+d)(a+b+e+f)}.
\]
After multiplication by the displayed positive denominators, the target numerator is
\[
(bce-adf)^2+R_{ADD},
\tag{12}
\]
where \(R_{ADD}\) has \(38\) monomials and every coefficient is a positive integer.  Equivalently, before combining the three indicated terms, the only negative monomial is \(-2abcdef\), while \(b^2c^2e^2\) and \(a^2d^2f^2\) both occur with coefficient \(1\).  This proves the \(ADD\) case.

We now prove the singleton type \(BDF\) without any algebraic expansion.  Relabel its vertices as \(V_i\), where \(V_i\) is in the singleton sector of \(H_i\); thus \(V_1\in F,V_2\in B,V_3\in D\).  The three vertex directions have every cyclic angular gap strictly smaller than \(\pi\), so the fan point \(O\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}T\).  Let
\[
(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)
\]
be its positive barycentric coordinates.

Consider any line through \(O\) which cuts off the vertex \(V_i\), and let \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\).  If its two edge ratios from \(V_i\) are \(s,t\), its equation in barycentric coordinates is
\[
\frac{x_j}{s}+\frac{x_k}{t}=1.
\]
Writing \(q=\lambda_j/s\), passage through \(O\) gives
\[
s=\frac{\lambda_j}{q},\qquad
t=\frac{\lambda_k}{1-q},\qquad
\lambda_j<q<1-\lambda_k.
\]
Hence the cap fraction is
\[
\frac{\lambda_j\lambda_k}{q(1-q)}.
\tag{13}
\]
Its infimum \(m_i\) over all such lines is therefore
\[
m_i=
\begin{cases}
4\lambda_j\lambda_k,&\lambda_j,\lambda_k\leq1/2,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle\frac{\lambda_k}{\lambda_i+\lambda_k},
&\lambda_j>1/2,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle\frac{\lambda_j}{\lambda_i+\lambda_j},
&\lambda_k>1/2.
\end{cases}
\tag{14}
\]
In particular, \(p_i\geq m_i\).

If \(\lambda_1>1/2\), then
\[
m_2=\frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_2+\lambda_3},
\qquad
m_3=\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_2+\lambda_3}=1-m_2.
\]
Thus
\[
(1-p_1)(1-p_2)\leq1-p_2\leq1-m_2=m_3\leq p_3.
\]
The case \(\lambda_2>1/2\) is symmetric.

Suppose next that \(\lambda_3>1/2\).  Then
\[
m_1=\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2},
\qquad
m_2=\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_1+\lambda_2}.
\]
Since \(p_1,p_2\leq1/2\), both inequalities can hold only if
\[
\lambda_1=\lambda_2,\qquad p_1=m_1=p_2=m_2=\frac12.
\]
The minimum in (14) is then attained only at the endpoint corresponding to a line through \(V_3\).  Consequently both \(\partial H_1\) and \(\partial H_2\) would be the line \(OV_3\), contradicting pairwise nonparallelity.  Hence this case cannot occur.

It remains that every \(\lambda_i\leq1/2\).  Put
\[
x=\lambda_1,\qquad y=\lambda_2,\qquad z=\lambda_3.
\]
Then
\[
m_1=4yz,\qquad m_2=4xz,\qquad m_3=4xy.
\]
Direct factorization gives
\[
m_3-(1-m_1)(1-m_2)
=-(2x+2y-1)
\bigl(8x^2y+8xy^2-12xy+2x+2y-1\bigr).
\tag{15}
\]
Here \(2x+2y-1=1-2z\geq0\).  The second factor in (15) equals
\[
1-2z-4xy(1+2z).
\]
Since \(x,y\leq1/2\) and \(x+y=1-z\), their product is minimized at
\(\{x,y\}=\{1/2,1/2-z\}\), so
\[
xy\geq\frac{1-2z}{4}.
\]
Therefore the second factor is nonpositive, and (15) is nonnegative.  Finally,
\[
p_3\geq m_3
\geq(1-m_1)(1-m_2)
\geq(1-p_1)(1-p_2).
\]
This proves the \(BDF\) type.

It remains only the \(BCF\) type.  Its exact fractions are
\[
p_1=\frac{(e+f)^2}{(a+e+f)(c+d+e+f)},
\]
\[
p_2=1-\frac{e^2}{(c+e)(a+b+e)},
\qquad
p_3=\frac{d^2}{(b+d)(d+f)}.
\tag{16}
\]
Scale all six parameters by \(1/e\), so \(e=1\).  The strict inequality \(p_2<1/2\) is equivalent to
\[
(1+c)(1+a+b)<2.
\tag{17}
\]
Consequently there are unique \(r,s,t>0\) such that
\[
c=\frac r{1+r},\qquad
\eta=\frac s{1+s},\qquad
a+b=\frac{1-c}{1+c}\eta,\qquad
\frac a{a+b}=\frac t{1+t}.
\tag{18}
\]
Write \(f=h>0\), \(W=1+h\), and put
\[
d_0=\frac{W(W-a)}{W+a}-c.
\tag{19}
\]
The strict inequality \(p_1<1/2\) is exactly \(d>d_0\), so write
\[
d=d_0+\rho,\qquad \rho>0.
\tag{20}
\]

For (16), set
\[
D_1=(a+W)(c+d+W),\qquad
D_2=(1+c)(1+a+b),\qquad
D_3=(b+d)(d+h).
\]
The common numerator (9) is now
\[
\Gamma=d^2D_1D_2-D_3\bigl(D_1-W^2\bigr).
\tag{21}
\]
Substitute (18)-(20) into (21) and put it over a common denominator.  That positive denominator is
\[
(1+r)^3(1+2r)^2(1+t)^2(1+s)^2
\left((1+2r)(1+h)(1+t)(1+s)+ts\right)^2.
\tag{22}
\]
The exact integer numerator has the coefficient certificate
\[
s^4t^2(1-ht)^2+R_{BCF},
\tag{23}
\]
where, after collecting like terms in
\(\mathbb Z[r,s,t,h,\rho]\), \(R_{BCF}\) has exactly \(4230\) distinct monomials and every coefficient is a positive integer.  The check is particularly transparent before collection: the only negative monomial is
\[
-2s^4t^3h,
\]
and the two corresponding positive monomials
\[
s^4t^2,\qquad s^4t^4h^2
\]
complete the square in (23); every remaining coefficient is positive.  Equations (18)-(23) are an exact symbolic identity obtained only by clearing the displayed positive denominators.  Thus \(\Gamma>0\) in the generic \(BCF\) case.

This completes all twelve generic types in (4).

We finally remove the genericity and strictness assumptions.  Choose a vector \(w\) in sector \(D\), so
\[
\ell _1(w)>0,\qquad \ell _2(w)>0,\qquad \ell _3(w)<0.
\]
For \(\varepsilon>0\), let
\[
T_\varepsilon=T+\varepsilon w.
\]
Its area is unchanged, and
\[
\left|T_\varepsilon\cap H_i\right|
=\left|T\cap\{\ell_i\leq-\varepsilon\ell_i(w)\}\right|
\qquad(i=1,2).
\]
Thus the first two cap fractions do not increase.  If either is \(1/2\), it becomes strictly smaller for every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), because a nondegenerate triangle has positive section length at every interior cutting level.  If it is \(0\), the direct argument at the start of the proof applies.

Choose a sequence \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\) avoiding the finitely many values for which a translated vertex lies on a fan line.  Since \(\ell_i(w)\ne0\) for all \(i\), an edge originally contained in a fan line is translated off that line as well.  Hence every \(T_{\varepsilon_n}\) is covered by the generic proof.  Halfplane-section areas of a fixed polygon depend continuously on translation, so letting \(n\to\infty\) gives
\[
p_3\geq(1-p_1)(1-p_2)
\]
for the original triangle.  This limit simultaneously covers a fan point outside, on an edge, or at a vertex of \(T\); vertices and edges on fan rays; empty caps; and half-full caps.  Multiplying by \(|T|^2\) proves
\[
c_3|T|\geq(|T|-c_1)(|T|-c_2).
\]
statement:
Let \(T\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a nondegenerate compact triangle, and let \(\ell _1,\ell _2,\ell _3\) be nonzero pairwise nonparallel linear forms satisfying
\[
\ell _1+\ell _2+\ell _3=0.
\]
Put
\[
c_i=\left|T\cap\{\ell_i\leq0\}\right|
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]
If
\[
c_1\leq\frac{|T|}{2},
\qquad
c_2\leq\frac{|T|}{2},
\]
then
\[
c_3|T|\geq (|T|-c_1)(|T|-c_2).
\]
This includes triangles for which the common fan point is outside \(T\), triangles having a vertex or an edge on a fan ray, and the cases \(c_i=0\) or \(c_i=|T|/2\).
